newsitem.title: UK: Fannie Mae's global stg bond steady at 8 b.p. over.
newsitem.headline: Fannie Mae's global stg bond steady at 8 b.p. over.

text.p: Fannie Mae's sterling global bond, the first of it kind, was holding steady at a spread of eight basis points over gilts at 1130 GMT on Friday, traders said.
This is two notches tighter than the launch spread of 10 b.p. over the 7.0 percent gilt due June 2002.
Fannie Mae launched the ground-breaking transaction on Tuesday, and it was priced on Wednesday via joint lead managers BZW and Merrill Lynch.
A syndicate official said there had been good two-way trade in the 1.0 billion stg bond, which was oversubscribed and saw a combined order book of 1.65 billion.

"We've had ongoing buying which is keeping the spread steady as more and more investors are attracted by the liquidity of the deal," he said, adding investors were encouraged by sterling's "safe-haven" status, unlikely to join European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) at the outset.
Sterling has appreciated by 15 percent against its trading partners on a trade-weighted basis since August.
Sales distribution at launch was 47 percent into Britain, 20 percent to Asian accounts, 18 percent into Continental Europe and 15 percent into the U.S.
"A lot of banks want to continue discussions with borrowers with the prospect of further sterling global transactions," a syndicate manager said. "The concept is now well-established."
